sources.entry: 4. Android App security best practices by Google

summary.title: Security checklist | Android Developers
summary.one_liner: Learn the core Android app security practices covering authentication, app integrity, data storage, permissions, networking, input validation, user data, WebView, credentials and API keys.
takeaways: Use Android's built-in sandbox and default permissions, and request only the permissions your app truly needs.
Keep internal storage private, avoid world-readable/writable modes, and never store sensitive data on external storage.
Set content providers to exported=false unless needed, use signature protection for same-developer sharing, and use parameterized queries.
Use HTTPS, avoid localhost IPC and SMS for sensitive data, and validate all untrusted input including WebView content.
Minimize user data and credential exposure, use Credential Manager/passkeys, and protect API keys with the Android Keystore.
summary.summary: This Android Developers page is a security checklist of best practices for building Android apps. It walks through the platform's built-in protections and then covers authentication, Play Integrity, data storage (internal, external, content providers), permissions, networking, input validation, user data, WebView, credential requests, and API key management. Each section pairs a common risk with concrete recommendations and the relevant Android APIs or manifest settings.
